synopsis: South Africa is the only jurisdiction the booklet found with a legal automatic slow-down and braking mandate for heavy mining machines: regulations published on 27 February 2015, suspended because technology was unavailable, commenced on 21 December 2022 with no transitional period [f164, f1363, f10724, f11457]. The rules require diesel-powered trackless mobile machines to detect and warn of collision risk, slow to a safe speed and brake automatically if the operator does not act, and fail to safe without human intervention; acceptance is by the mine operator against the regulation, using industry guidelines as reference [f2079, f2080, f1367]. The mandate preceded validation standards and specifies no detection percentage, distance, false-alarm limit or stopping-distance test; subsequent industry documents include independent verification specifications dated 29 August 2025, a verification regime dated 11 October 2025 and a TRL7 stage-gate specification dated 20 January 2026 [f1360, f2081, f555, f556, f557]. The MOSH surface specification adds a 200 m minimum detection range, warning 2.5–3.0 seconds before intervention, fail-to-safe within 500 ms, defined stop gaps and no false interventions at TRL4, while Pretoria testing reported pass rates of 62% for detection devices, 42% for machine-side systems and 83% for third-party interfaces across 189 tests [f174, f175, f177, f176, f178, f5178]. Safety concerns persist: total mining fatalities fell from 55 in 2023 to 42 in 2024, but trackless-mobile-machine deaths rose from six to nine in 2024; guidance also warns that a fixed stop gap would make truck loading impossible [f3138, f3008, f3023]. Planning should distinguish mandatory Level 9 deployment from vendor advice to evaluate without immediately enforcing intervention, recognize conflicting trade reporting about commencement, and not assume simulation can replace prescribed physical tests [f358, f6575, f1364, f2103].

relations.note: Both identify South Africa as the only jurisdiction found mandating automatic slowing and braking.
Both report no other identified legal mandate.
Both date independent verification specifications to 29 August 2025.
Both date the TRL7 stage-gate specification to 20 January 2026.
Both state that the legal mandate preceded validation standards.
Both require diesel TMM slowing then automatic braking when the operator does not act.
Both require fail-to-safe without human intervention.
Both give 21 December 2022 as the regulations' commencement date.
Both describe 2015 publication and December 2022 commencement without transition.
Duplicate accounts of the 2015 suspension because technology was unavailable.
Both identify missing regulatory performance thresholds; Chapter 3 additionally names distance.
The guidance's 10% g response-time definition drives the actuator-identification recommendation.
Immediate Level 9 requirements pushed deployment followed by refinement.
Vendor advice delays enforcement, whereas South Africa mandates Level 9 without transition.
Reported December 2023 timing conflicts with documented December 2022 commencement.
Uneven verification pass rates support the account of systems needing refinement.
Operational loading constraints qualify how defined stop gaps can be implemented.
